title: Hybrid admission, soft-burst profiles, and elevated telemetry for hosted GPU hyperdrain incidents
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Post-incident follow-up for a hosted API GPU exhaustion event that produced multi-tenant queue buildup and aggressive throttling. This ticket captures the hybrid admission strategy (stratified admission + soft-burst profiles), telemetry elevation, and automated smoke tests needed to prevent recurrence and speed diagnosis. Goal: reduce frequency of hyperdrain events and shorten time-to-recovery by improving signals and safe degradation behaviors.
investigation_summary: During the outage we observed sustained prefetch amplification from a small subset of tenants, an autoscaler hysteresis window that delayed replenishment by ~90s, and admission thresholds tuned for steady-state throughput which failed under bursty arrival patterns. KV cache misses amplified compute time for long-context requests. The runtime's admission logic treated all requests equally causing long-running high-priority jobs to starve short interactive requests. Metrics show tail latency spikes correlated with sustained queue depth > 120 per GPU for more than 2 minutes before throttling began.
root_causes: Admission thresholds optimized for median load, not bursty tail conditions
Autoscaler cool-down hysteresis too long for short-lived surges
Prefetch behavior amplified tenant bursts (no per-tenant prefetch caps)
Insufficient telemetry around per-tenant queue lengths and KV cache hit-rate for served shards
action_items: (Marco Liu) Implement stratified admission logic: classify requests into latency buckets and enforce per-bucket slot caps. Due: 2025-02-28
(Aisha Patel) Add soft-burst profiles: allow short, bounded burst tokens for interactive routes with fast decay. Due: 2025-02-20
(DevOps: Priya Rangan) Reduce autoscaler cool-down and add opportunistic prewarm path for high variance queues. Due: 2025-03-07
(Telemetry: Jon Kim) Elevate per-tenant queue length, per-shard KV cache hit-rate, and admission decision logs to platform dashboards + alerting. Due: 2025-02-14
(SRE: Elena Torres) Create GPU hyperdrain synthetic test harness and daily smoke run as part of CI. Due: 2025-02-21
(PM: Ravi Shah) Update runbook with soft-fallback rollout and tenant throttling playbook. Due: 2025-02-18
acceptance_criteria: Stratified admission deployed to canary; canary shows <30% queue-depth incidents over 72h under synthetic burst tests
Soft-burst profiles allow short interactive bursts without causing autoscaler triggers; validated in staging
Telemetry dashboards show per-tenant queue and KV hit-rate within 1 minute of occurrence; alert fires when queue > 80 for > 60s
Autoscaler adjustments reduce time-to-scale median from ~90s to <40s in synthetic tests
Synthetic daily smoke detects regressions (fail fast) and test results are visible in build artifacts
tests_and_validation: Create synthetic burst generator: multi-tenant traffic with 95th-99.9th percentile patterns (200 tenants, 30% heavy).
Run experiments comparing current admission vs stratified admission under identical burst traffic for 6h windows.
KV cache warm/cold tests to measure miss amplification and validate cache-awareness in admission decisions.
Chaos scenario: temporarily disable prewarm path to measure graceful degradation and fallback correctness.
